cards.prompt: Long coach trip, no charger. Make the battery last **at least 8 hours**, and keep your **music** playing. (**Low power mode** is a setting that makes the phone save energy.)
cards.explanation: The biggest drains are usually **screen brightness**, **location** and **apps busy in the background**. Turning those down or off (or using **low power mode**) stretches the battery. Music on its own uses very little.
cards.hint: Change one setting at a time and watch the power meter. Which one makes the biggest difference? Keep the music on.
cards.nudge: Music uses very little power, so it can stay on. Find the settings that make the power meter drop the most.

cards.prompt: Batteries hate **heat**: it wears them out faster, so they hold less charge. Does each habit **help** the battery, or **drain or damage** it?

items.label: Low power mode on a long day
Keeping it out of the hot sun
Leaving it in a hot car
Location on for every app, all day

cards.explanation: Lower brightness and low power mode save charge. **Heat** wears a battery out: hot cars and charging under a pillow (which traps heat) are bad news. Location on all day keeps draining it.
cards.hint: Two things hurt a battery: heavy use, like location on all day, and **heat**. Which habits save energy or keep it cool?
cards.nudge: Heat trapped while charging counts too. Settings that save energy help; anything left running all day drains it.

cards.prompt: You plug your phone in before bed, but the charging symbol doesn't appear. Good to know: cables and chargers wear out far more often than phones, and **metal or water** in a charging [[port]] can damage it.

steps.text: What's the simplest thing to try first?

choices.text: Try a different cable and a different plug socket
choices.consequence: Good: cables and chargers wear out far more often than phones do.

choices.text: Poke a pin into the charging port to clean it
choices.consequence: Never put metal in the port. It can scratch the contacts or cause a [[short circuit]].

steps.text: The other cable charges a friend's phone, but still not yours. With a torch you can see the port is **packed with pocket fluff**.

choices.text: Phone off, get an adult to help brush it out with a soft, dry brush
choices.consequence: Out comes the fluff, and the cable clicks in properly. It's charging! If it hadn't worked, a repair shop could clean it safely.

choices.text: Dig the fluff out carefully with a paper clip
choices.consequence: Metal can damage the port or short it out. Use something soft, or let a repair shop do it.

choices.text: Rinse the fluff out of the port with water
choices.consequence: Water and electronics don't mix. It could damage the phone for good.

cards.explanation: Start with the simplest fix: **another cable and socket**. Fluff in the port is common: with the phone off, an adult can gently brush it out with something soft and dry. **Never metal, never water.** If in doubt, a repair shop can do it.
cards.hint: Start with the simplest, safest fix. For fluff, think soft, dry and a grown-up's help.

cards.prompt: Tap the **charging port**, where the fluff was hiding.
cards.explanation: The **charging port** is on the bottom edge. It's open to the outside, which is why pocket fluff collects in it.
cards.hint: It's where the charger plugs in, and it's open to the outside. Check the edges of the phone.
cards.nudge: Think about where you plug a charger into a phone. That opening is on the outside, along one of its edges.

cards.prompt: A tablet won't charge, and its port looks fluffy. Is each idea **safe to try** or could it **damage** the tablet?

items.label: Tablet off, adult uses a soft, dry brush
Take it to a repair shop
Poke the fluff out with a pin
Scrape it out with a paper clip
Rinse the port under the tap

cards.explanation: Cables and sockets first, then something **soft and dry** with an adult's help, or a repair shop. **Metal** can scratch the contacts or cause a [[short circuit]], and **water** can damage the tablet for good.
cards.hint: Remember the two things that must never go in a port. Everything else here is gentle.
cards.nudge: Pins and paper clips are both metal. Water is just as risky. Soft, dry and gentle is the rule.

cards.title: When a battery swells
cards.body:
Phones and laptops use **lithium-ion** batteries. Very old or damaged ones can **swell**: the case bulges, the screen lifts at one edge, or a laptop's trackpad (the touch pad) gets pushed up.

A swollen battery can catch fire if it's pressed or punctured. Stop using the device, don't press it, and get help from an adult or a repair shop.

cards.prompt: An old laptop's case is **bulging**, and the trackpad is being pushed up from underneath. What should you do?

options.text: Stop using it, unplug it, and tell an adult
Press the case flat so the trackpad works
options.nudge: Pressing is the risky part. A swollen battery can catch fire if it's pressed or punctured, so hands off.

options.text: Keep using it, as long as it still turns on
options.nudge: Turning on doesn't mean it's safe. A bulge can mean the battery is swelling, and that's not something to keep using.

cards.explanation: A bulge often means the **battery is swelling**. A swollen [[lithium battery|lithium-ion]] can catch fire if it's pressed, bent or punctured. Stop using it, unplug it, keep it away from anything that can burn, and **tell an adult**. A repair shop can replace the battery safely.
cards.hint: A bulging case often means something inside is swelling. What did the last card say is dangerous to do to a swollen battery?

cards.prompt: You're gaming on your bed with the phone plugged in.

steps.text: The phone is really hot, and a message says **"Phone needs to cool down."**

choices.text: Put it in the freezer to cool it quickly
choices.consequence: Sudden cold can make water droplets form inside the phone. Let it cool down slowly.

choices.text: Ignore it and keep playing until the level ends
choices.consequence: The phone will slow down to protect itself, and all that heat wears out the battery.

choices.text: Stop, unplug it and leave it on a table out of the sun
choices.consequence: It cools down safely in a few minutes.

steps.text: A week later, the back of the phone looks **puffed up** and the screen is lifting at one edge.

choices.text: Stop using it and get it to a repair shop with an adult's help
choices.consequence: A puffed-up phone often has a swollen battery. A repair shop can replace it safely.
Pressing on a swollen battery can make it catch fire. Leave it alone and get help.

cards.explanation: An overheating phone needs to **stop, unplug and cool down slowly** on a hard surface out of the sun. Never freeze it. A phone that looks puffed up may have a **swollen battery**: stop using it, don't press it, and get help from an adult or a repair shop.
cards.hint: Heat and batteries don't mix, and sudden cold isn't the answer either. Cool it gently, and if something looks swollen, hands off.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- **Brightness, location and background apps** drain batteries most. **Heat** wears them out.
- Won't charge? Another cable first. Never metal or water in the port.
- Bulging device? Stop using it, don't press it, get help.
